## Working session summary

I've finished issue #31: the app can now find personal contacts you haven't talked to for 90+ days and prepare the right message for each. PR #34 is ready for review, CI passes (including tests on node, bun and deno across Linux, macOS and Windows), and it can be merged cleanly: https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/pull/34

**What it does**
- **Finding contacts:** it looks for one-to-one chats with no message for at least 90 days, in either direction. Groups, channels and bots are left out, and you must have written to the person at least once, so unanswered spam doesn't count.
- **"ты" or "вы":** a set of word-level regex rules decides which form the dialog used. Your own messages count twice, because the new message is yours.
  - The screen shows the evidence for the guess and lets you flip it with one click or key.
  - A tie or no evidence falls back to "вы", which is safer than an unexpected "ты".
  - On "our rules": you can add your own rules as patterns labelled informal or formal, with no code changes.
- **Texts:** the two texts from the issue are the defaults. You can replace them, and `{name}` is filled in with the contact's name.
- **Safe mode is the default everywhere:** one prefilled, editable message at a time, sent only after you confirm. A failed send stays on the same message.
  - "Send all" exists only when you switch safe mode off, and it still asks once.
  - In the API, the batch route refuses unless you pass `mode: "batch"` and `confirm: true`.
- **Three ways to use it:**
  - a new **Re-engage** screen in the app;
  - `meta-sovereign reengage`, with `--interactive` to go one by one;
  - HTTP routes: `/api/reengage/plan`, `/send`, `/mark` and `/run`.
- **No repeats:** every send, skip and failure is remembered, so the same person isn't offered again until another 90 days pass.
- **Manual sending:** where the app can't send, each message has Copy, an "Open chat" link and "I sent it myself".

**Checks.** Locally, all 551 tests pass, along with lint, formatting and the duplication check; the logs are saved in the case study folder. I tested the screen in a real browser against a demo server with a fake sender, covering sending, skipping, a failed send and "Send all". The four screenshots are in the PR description.

**Things you should know**
- **Server:** sending from the app needs the JS server. The Rust server doesn't have these routes; that gap is recorded in the server-parity doc. Without a server, the list and the manual-send options still work.
- **Telegram:** imported contacts are numeric ids, so "Open chat" opens the chat but can't prefill the text. Telegram's documented `t.me/<username>?text=` link would allow it once an importer records usernames. I also haven't checked how real Telegram apps handle these id-based links.
- **VK:** VK's official docs couldn't be fetched from here, so the rule for telling personal chats from group chats is cross-checked only against community sources, such as [this Habr answer](https://qna.habr.com/q/604802) and [the vk-io helpers reference](https://www.mintlify.com/negezor/vk-io/api-reference/helpers).
- **Languages:** detection rules ship for Russian, Chinese and Hindi only. Others, like German du/Sie, can be added as patterns.
- **Moved folder:** `docs/case-studies/issue-31/` already held a case study about the pipeline template's issue 31. I moved it unchanged to `docs/case-studies/pipeline-template-issue-31/` to make room for this one.

I also added the requirements, a new user-guide section and server-parity notes, all in English, Russian, Chinese and Hindi. Alongside them are a case study in `docs/case-studies/issue-31/` and a changeset for a minor release.

Instead of separate screen for it we should make it like scheduler or manual trigger, see triggers concept from https://github.com/konard/vk-bot

We don't need separate chat for or screen, just regular chat is enough.

So that should be part of preexisting features. We should focus on producing more universal configurable solutions, not specific features that are not changeable by user.

Yet such talking strategy can help user find jobs or contracts.

In chat we should use our message to massage database (which should be learnable from vk archive or API or real time in dialogs).

We should use latest associative stack for all the systems and especially for storage, import and export (text + binary) links notation, and for fast search and access - link-cli database.

https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/main/docs/associative-tech-stack.md - here details.

We need update exactly all dependencies we have.

Also take best experience from https://github.com/konard/hh-job-application-automation

So the idea for this is automations.

Automation can be triggered manually on selected users (which should be searchable, and cross referenced), for example we can search for audiences - each audience can be merged from lists, communities, chats and so on, for example we can configure intersect multiple lists of users to make sure we have exactly people we need.

And for such audience we can trigger the automation.

Automation can be triggered for all friends, people from chat, community and so on directly with conditions, like we only send hi/hello to users we didn't talked for 90 days.

Automation can also be triggered via menu inside each private chat or group chat to test it.

We also need to make sure we use message to message (replies mapping) for autocomplete, if single message has multiple possible answers we used before we show deduplicated list of them sorted by frequency of previous usage for each message to message reply link.

For that link-cli should be used, to do it fast.

If no messages directly match last message in the chat, we can do autocomplete word by word based on our message history by default only by our own messages.

So we try first autocomplete by entire message, if no matches we go to word by word autocomplete, so we speed up user's typing time.

We also must fully support typing status in all messangers, meaning when user or automation is typing we show that status for that again see https://github.com/konard/vk-bot

The style of default UI/UX for chats should be closer to https://t3.codes with option to switch to telegram like theme (source code also is present on the internet), prefer to reuse best practices and not reinvent the wheel, yet we still need everything to be in React.js

So we need automatic dark/light/system or auto themes, and multiple supported skins based on best messaging apps we have source code of.

Double check exactly all my requirements are fully delivered.

We also need to make our message sending/receiving fully advanced, so if we cannot do it directly via API, we should use official web UI of VK, telegram and others via our https://github.com/link-foundation/browser-commander, so if API fails or not available we fallback to sending via browser.

Please plan and execute everything in this single pull request, you have unlimited time and context, as context auto-compacts and you can continue indefinitely, until each and every requirement fully addressed, and everything is totally done.
